title: A bill to nullify the Supplemental Treaty Between the United States of America and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of Indians of Middle Oregon, concluded on November 15, 1865.
official_summary: This bill nullifies the supplemental treaty between the United States and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of Indians of Middle Oregon signed in 1865. The treaty restricted the rights of tribal members to leave the reservation and imposed other conditions. The Department of the Interior has stated that the treaty has never been enforced by the federal government or Oregon.

summary.headline: This 2020 law cancels an 1865 supplemental treaty between the United States and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of Indians of Middle Oregon.
summary.what_it_does: The law declares the 1865 supplemental treaty nullified, meaning it no longer has legal force. The treaty had limited tribal members' ability to leave the reservation and set other conditions. According to the Department of the Interior, the federal government and the state of Oregon never enforced the treaty.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Confederated Tribes and Bands of Indians of Middle Oregon
who_it_affects.how: The 1865 treaty's restrictions on leaving the reservation and other conditions no longer apply to them.

who_it_affects.group: The federal government and the state of Oregon
who_it_affects.how: They are no longer bound by the 1865 supplemental treaty's terms.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 20, 2020; the summary does not describe a separate effective date.
